The QUIET Act (H.R. 1027) claims to crack down on AI robocalls by mandating disclosures upfront and doubling penalties for impersonation scams. But let’s cut through the noise: Washington’s failure to protect seniors from predatory tactics isn’t new. Medicare Advantage beneficiaries get bombarded because bureaucrats let telecom giants off the hook while writing toothless regulations.

The bill’s Section 3 boosts fines, but when the FCC’s own data shows 50+ billion robocalls annually, doubling penalties for a fraction of cases is bureaucratic theater. Meanwhile, Medicare fraudsters still siphon $60B yearly from taxpayers.

Real solutions? Crush the telecom loopholes letting foreign call centers spoof numbers and mandate carriers block ALL unverified calls by default—not another performative disclosure regime. Until D.C. stops treating symptoms instead of the disease, seniors will keep drowning in roboscams.
